summary.business: Bharat Forge designs, manufactures, and tests forged and machined components, primarily for automotive (commercial and passenger vehicles), industrial (oil & gas, power, construction, mining, data centers), aerospace, and defense applications. The company serves leading global OEMs with a focus on safety-critical parts for engines, drivelines, and transmissions, while also expanding into defense platforms, unmanned vehicles, and aerospace sub-assemblies. Its integrated capabilities span from product engineering to validation, supported by a diversified global manufacturing footprint.

Industrial: Forged and machined components for semiconductor manufacturing equipment

currentContext.strategies: Prioritize safety-critical components across Engines, Driveline and Transmission systems to remain a critical supplier to OEMs.|Expand market share and introduce new parts in PV exports, prioritizing markets where electrification is less relevant, aiming to be the last man standing for ICE components.|Diversify the Industrial business across end-user industries and geographies to offset sector- and country-specific volatilities.|Leverage AI-led data centre boom for backup power engine components and take steps towards supplying forged and machined components for semiconductor manufacturing equipment.|Financial prudence and operational focus (Strategy S5). currentContext.expansion: Bharat Forge's expansion narrative is centered on its subsidiary JS Auto Cast (JSA), which has a total liquid metal capacity of 130,000 MTPA. The recent acquisition K Drive Mobility Solutions is developing its Axles portfolio beyond M&HCVs, with new programmes expected to enter production in 2-3 years. The Defence business anticipates a reversal of a temporary blip in FY27 as execution for ATAGS and Carbine orders commences.

risks.risk: Transition from IC engine to E-mobility
risks.note: Large-scale global transition across PV and M&HCV has the potential to materially alter the company's growth ambitions.
Trade tariffs and non-tariff barriers can escalate costs and alter competitive advantages for certain geographies or products.
Disruptions of sea-routes and challenges to navigation in open seas pose logistics and supply chain risk.
In an inter-connected environment, any breach of secure networks has the potential to impact competitive advantages.
Significant portion of revenue is derived from exports, and some items are imported, exposing the company to foreign exchange risk.
Shortage of skilled workforce impacts the company's growth plans.
Increasing need to continuously adapt to evolving technologies to meet changing customer expectations and sustain competitiveness.

one-line thesis: Bharat Forge pivots aggressively toward high-margin defense (INR 11k cr order book) and aerospace (26% of non-auto exports), offsetting standalone auto headwinds and EV slowdowns. Management guides for ~25% India growth in FY27 driven by defense production ramps and new machining acquisitions, while restructuring loss-making European steel assets to stop cash bleed.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 16,812 cr (+11% YoY); EBITDA: INR 2,921 cr (+6% YoY, margin ~17.4%); PAT: Not explicitly stated but PBT before exceptional items INR 1,826 cr (-8% YoY); Order Book: Defense ~INR 11,000 cr, New Business Wins FY26 INR 4,814 cr; Net Debt/Equity: 0.41x consolidated, 0.18x standalone. One-offs: INR 11 cr retrospective power sub-cess charge in Q4; INR 12 cr tariff impact absorbed; Write-offs on non-viable e-mobility investments.
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~25% for India operations in FY27; Margins: Aerospace > company average, K-Drive target mid-teens; Order Inflow: Strong defense ramp (ATAGS, CQB Carbine) starting H2 FY27; Capex: INR 800-850 cr over next 15-18 months.
order book & pipeline: Defense order book stands at ~INR 11,000 cr covering next 3-4 years. New business wins in FY26 totaled INR 4,814 cr (Defense: INR 2,816 cr; Traditional: INR 1,210 cr; JSA: INR 292 cr; K-Drive: INR 500 cr).
segment / subsidiary detail: Standalone Revenue INR 8,396 cr (-5% YoY) due to US CV demand/regulatory issues, but Q4 rebounded +8.5% QoQ. Europe Revenue INR 3,865 cr (4% margin); US Revenue INR 1,534 cr (3.5% margin). Aerospace FY26 revenue ~INR 400 cr, now 26% of Q4 non-auto industrial exports. Defense FY26 revenue INR 1,562 cr.
growth verticals / optionality: Defense: ATAGS and CQB Carbine production ramping H2 FY27; new drone/naval orders. Aerospace: Targeting >INR 1,000 cr run rate within 3 years. Machining: Fortuna acquisition (30% stake) opens large connecting rod market. Data Center: Supplying auxiliaries/power components, though not a core server play.
margins & cost dynamics: Pressure from energy costs (negotiating pass-through); Q4 margin 27% (standalone) impacted by INR 11 cr one-off (would have been 28%). Overseas margins low (EU 4%, US 3.5%) due to restructuring and weak demand. Aerospace margins above company average. K-Drive/Fortuna targeting mid-teens.
capex / expansion: INR 800-850 cr planned over 15-18 months across forging, casting, and product platforms. New explosives facility in Andhra Pradesh breaking ground soon (24-month timeline to pilot production). Orissa project environmental clearance pending (2-4 months).
capital allocation: Active M&A: Acquired 30% Fortuna Engineering (INR 130 cr), full K-Drive integration. JSA raised external capital from Premji Invest to fuel independent expansion. Evaluating further India M&A in auto/aerospace. Potential future listing of defense subsidiary (KSSL) under consideration.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical instability (Middle East war impact on logistics/markets); Delay in ATAGS production approvals; Continued losses in European subsidiaries until restructuring completes (end CY27); EV adoption slower than anticipated globally; Energy cost volatility.
management quality / tone: Confident on India defense/aerospace trajectory; Pragmatic on EV (admitting strategy recalibration/write-offs); Transparent on overseas struggles (restructuring CDP Germany); Aggressive on inorganic growth (M&A) to accelerate capacity.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly stated EV adoption trajectory has diverged from expectations, leading to write-offs of non-immediate revenue projects. Aerospace is now the second largest contributor to industrial exports, surpassing traditional expectations. Data center play is limited to auxiliaries/power, not server manufacturing.

themes.title: Defence indigenization & order-book visibility
themes.need: Indigenization mandates (IDDM / Atmanirbhar / DcPP) plus multi-year order books make domestic defence the cleanest revenue-conversion theme - across electronics, drones, simulators, explosives/munitions and precision systems. BEL guides >INR55k cr FY27 inflow (~INR30k cr QRSAM pending CCS clearance, guided by September) on a INR72,258cr order book; HAL book ~INR2.55 lakh cr; SOLARINDS defence revenue +94% to INR2,634cr FY26, guided >INR4,500cr FY27 on an ~INR18,000cr defence order book (Bhargavastra counter-drone trials completing CY2026); DATAPATTNS inflows strong; BHARATFORG/BEML add land-systems and platforms.
themes.driver: Backlog-to-revenue conversion underway; BEL's QRSAM CCS clearance (guided by Sep-2026, ~INR30k cr of the FY27 inflow guide) is the load-bearing near-term catalyst; fresh MoD orders + emergency procurement; HAL LCA Mk-1A ramp (gated on GE engines).

themes.title: Commercial-aerospace supply chain (Boeing/Airbus/engine OEMs)
themes.need: A record global commercial-aircraft backlog plus engine-OEM (GE/Safran/Honeywell/RR/P&W) outsourcing and China+1 are pulling Indian build-to-print suppliers up the value chain - aero-engine hot-section airfoils, airframe structures, tooling and wire harnesses. AZAD ramping engine/airfoil exports; UNIMECH near-tripling tooling capacity; AEQUS/SANSERA on precision aero; ROSSTECH on harnesses; PTCIL on titanium castings.
themes.driver: New commercial-aero RFP wins; engine-component capacity ramps; new MRO licences; Boeing/Airbus build-rate recovery.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Bharat Forge designs, manufactures, and tests forged and machined components, primarily for automotive (commercial and passenger vehicles), industrial (oil & gas, power, construction, mining, data centers), aerospace, and defense applications. The company serves leading global OEMs with a focus on safety-critical parts for engines, drivelines, and transmissions, while also expanding into defense platforms, unmanned vehicles, and aerospace sub-assemblies. Its integrated capabilities span from product engineering to validation, supported by a diversified global manufacturing footprint.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Kalyani Strategic Systems Limited — subsidiary: Houses the defense business; won major orders for underwater systems and CQB carbines.
- JS Autocast — subsidiary: Iron casting capacity; received primary equity investment for new Foundry and Machining capacity.
- BF Industrial Technology & Solutions — subsidiary: Steel forging capacity.
- K Drive Mobility — subsidiary: Acquired for engineering know-how in axle design across LCV, SUV segments and E-mobility platforms.
- Agneyastra Energetics — subsidiary: Commenced groundbreaking for Explosives & Propellants facility in Andhra Pradesh.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Standalone Revenue INR 8,396 cr (-5% YoY) due to US CV demand/regulatory issues, but Q4 rebounded +8.5% QoQ. Europe Revenue INR 3,865 cr (4% margin); US Revenue INR 1,534 cr (3.5% margin). Aerospace FY26 revenue ~INR 400 cr, now 26% of Q4 non-auto industrial exports. Defense FY26 revenue INR 1,562 cr.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Automotive:** Engine components, Driveline components, Transmission components, Safety-critical components for CV and PV
- **Industrial:** Engine components for backup power, Chassis components, Transmission components, Forged and machined components for semiconductor manufacturing equipment
- **Defense:** CQB Carbines, ATAGS (Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System), Unmanned Underwater Vehicles, Vikram VT21 8x8 armored platform, Naval guns, Transmission & steering systems for ships, Propulsion components for ship engines, Underwater training modules, Propellants and Explosives
- **Aerospace:** Aerostructures, Landing gear systems, Critical engine components, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), Titanium grade Landing Gear for UAVs
- **Industrial (Ferrous Castings):** Complex castings for Wind Energy, Hydraulics, Construction & Mining, Agriculture, Automobiles

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Defense order book stands at ~INR 11,000 cr covering next 3-4 years. New business wins in FY26 totaled INR 4,814 cr (Defense: INR 2,816 cr; Traditional: INR 1,210 cr; JSA: INR 292 cr; K-Drive: INR 500 cr).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: ~25% for India operations in FY27; Margins: Aerospace > company average, K-Drive target mid-teens; Order Inflow: Strong defense ramp (ATAGS, CQB Carbine) starting H2 FY27; Capex: INR 800-850 cr over next 15-18 months.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Defense: ATAGS and CQB Carbine production ramping H2 FY27; new drone/naval orders. Aerospace: Targeting >INR 1,000 cr run rate within 3 years. Machining: Fortuna acquisition (30% stake) opens large connecting rod market. Data Center: Supplying auxiliaries/power components, though not a core server play.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- We expect the industrials segment (ex-Defense) to post strong performance as construction activity gains momentum and private capex grows.
- The tremendous tailwinds generated by the AI-led demand will translate into strong growth for the backup power engine components vertical.
- We expect the semiconductor manufacturing equipment component segment to show positive momentum given the current boom.
- The current tariff regime in the US has resulted in no business disruptions as well as no impact on market share for Bharat Forge.
- In the medium term, our focus is geared towards expanding market share, introducing new parts and prioritizing markets where the electrification trend is less relevant.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Pressure from energy costs (negotiating pass-through); Q4 margin 27% (standalone) impacted by INR 11 cr one-off (would have been 28%). Overseas margins low (EU 4%, US 3.5%) due to restructuring and weak demand. Aerospace margins above company average. K-Drive/Fortuna targeting mid-teens.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Active M&A: Acquired 30% Fortuna Engineering (INR 130 cr), full K-Drive integration. JSA raised external capital from Premji Invest to fuel independent expansion. Evaluating further India M&A in auto/aerospace. Potential future listing of defense subsidiary (KSSL) under consideration.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Bharat Forge's expansion narrative is centered on its subsidiary JS Auto Cast (JSA), which has a total liquid metal capacity of 130,000 MTPA. During the year, JSA undertook numerous de-bottlenecking projects and streamlined operations to optimise costs. To increase value-add, JSA has optimised its Machining capacity. The recent acquisition K Drive Mobility Solutions is developing its Axles portfolio beyond M&HCVs, with new programmes expected to enter production in 2-3 years. The Defence business anticipates a reversal of a temporary blip in FY27 as execution for ATAGS and Carbine orders commences.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on India defense/aerospace trajectory; Pragmatic on EV (admitting strategy recalibration/write-offs); Transparent on overseas struggles (restructuring CDP Germany); Aggressive on inorganic growth (M&A) to accelerate capacity.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Critical supplier status with major global OEMs, ensuring long-lasting engagements and no business disruptions or market share loss despite US tariffs.
- Diversified customer base and geographic presence across automotive, industrial, aerospace, and defense sectors, offsetting sector- and country-specific volatilities.
- Integrated capabilities from design and product engineering to manufacturing, testing, and validation, enabling a shift up the value chain towards sub-assemblies and systems.
- Strong position in the Indian defense sector with IP ownership at the core of its product portfolio, maximizing exports and tempering cyclicality.
- Beneficiary of the AI-led data center boom as a major engine components supplier for backup power plants.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Defence order] Largest-ever naval order signed in the quarter — 12 Marine Gas Turbine Generator sets for the Ministry of Defence — against a Defence outstanding orderbook of Rs 11,196 Crore as of 30th June 2026.
- [Restructuring] Restructuring actions have already been taken on the EV business and the German Forging business, with exceptional items of Rs -3,335 million at Overseas Operations and Rs -245 million at Indian Operations in Q1 FY27 (consolidated Rs -3,580 million).
- [Consolidation change] "K Drive Mobility is consolidated within Indian Operation w.e.f 1st July 2025. YoY Indian Operations results for Q1FY27 are not comparable", and separately "Q1FY26 result does not include K-Drive and hence YoY results are not comparable" — so consolidated and Indian-operations YoY comparisons in this deck are not like-for-like.
- [Macro] Management frames the quarter against "spiraling energy prices and geopolitical uncertainty", with the export rebound tied to a North American truck cycle recovery and inventory restocking rather than structural demand.
